messages:
acme-frontend: Hey team, we're seeing intermittent 401s from Redwood when our Next.js app runs on Vercel Edge. Happens ~1-2% of requests, only in prod, no issues locally.

acme-frontend: Symptoms: streaming response stops, SDK call returns 401, subsequent immediate retry succeeds. No obvious CORS preflight failures.

acme-frontend: Here's minimal repro we used on a failing deploy (Edge runtime):
```ts
// client.ts
fetch('/api/redwood-proxy', {
  method: 'POST',
  credentials: 'include',
  keepalive: true,
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }),
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }
})
```

acme-frontend: Serverless edge handler uses edge-sdk v0.8.1 (installed), calls Redwood.generate streaming with keepalive turned on.

elaine: Thanks — can you paste the SDK version from package-lock and the exact failing request headers (including Authorization redacted)?

acme-frontend: package-lock shows "@redwood/edge-sdk": "0.8.1". Failing request headers (auth token redacted):
```
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
origin: https://app.acme.com
accept: text/event-stream
```

raj: Do you have any service worker or proxy altering headers? Also, is the auth token rotated frequently?

acme-frontend: No service worker. Token is static for this session. We also logged that when keepalive:true + streaming the Authorization header is occasionally missing when it reaches Redwood (trace id included below).

support-bot: Ticket #SR-2042 created — please attach a trace id and example timestamps.

acme-frontend: Example trace id: trace=abc123-def456. Failing request at 2026-03-15T18:42:01Z, retry at 18:42:01.120 succeeded.

sam: Quick hypothesis: Vercel edge runtime uses an internal fetch behavior that can buffer/merge requests with keepalive, and older edge-sdk versions used a wrapper that didn't re-attach auth on retries. Can you confirm whether retry logic is happening in the SDK or on the platform side?

acme-frontend: It looks like the SDK is configured with automatic retries on 5xx, but we see 401s — the retry seems immediate and succeeds. The SDK logs show: "attempt 1 -> 401" then "attempt 2 -> 200".

elaine: If the SDK replays the request from a background worker without the original Request object, Authorization can get lost if it's not explicitly copied. Can you enable DEBUG logs for the edge-sdk and paste lines around the failure?

acme-frontend: Pasting redacted logs (timestamps simplified):
```
[edge-sdk] request:start id=abc123 method=POST url=/v1/generate
[edge-sdk] request:headers id=abc123 Authorization=*** present
[edge-sdk] response:status id=abc123 status=401
[edge-sdk] retry:replaying id=abc123
[edge-sdk] request:headers id=abc123 Authorization=undefined
[edge-sdk] response:status id=abc123 status=200
```

raj: That confirms Authorization dropped during replay. Two likely causes: 1) SDK version bug that doesn't copy headers on replay for keepalive streams, 2) Edge runtime fetch polyfill behavior when keepalive present. We should test with the latest SDK that fixed header-copying on retries.

sam: Can you try upgrading to edge-sdk 0.9.3 (the version that included request cloning fix) as a quick experiment? If you can't upgrade, a workaround is to set retry:0 or explicitly pass credentials on each replay by using a wrapper that injects auth into request init.

acme-frontend: Will try upgrade. Question: will this affect our streaming behavior or cause double-charges? We have bursty traffic.

elaine: Upgrading shouldn't change token usage. The fix ensures the header is preserved. If you disable retries, you'll avoid double requests but may surface transient 5xx. For streaming, the newer SDK has safer clone semantics.

acme-frontend: Rolled upgrade to 0.9.3 on a canary with same deploy URL. After 6k requests, no 401s seen so far. Will monitor.

acme-frontend: Quick note — we also tried a curl repro from our CI to mimic Vercel edge streaming:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
It always preserved auth (so problem seems specific to Vercel + old SDK).

raj: Thanks for the confirm. We'll also add instrumentation to log when a request replay happens and whether headers were present. @deploy-bot can you link the rollout note to the SDK change?

deploy-bot: Release created: edge-sdk@0.9.3 — changelog: 'fix: preserve headers on replay for keepalive/streaming requests' (PR #378).

support-bot: Updating ticket #SR-2042 -> status: customer verifying upgraded SDK; assign to eng-runtime for follow-up.

elaine: If any other customers hit this, we should add a KB article: 'Intermittent 401s from edge runtime on Vercel — upgrade edge-sdk to >=0.9.3 or disable retries'.

acme-frontend: Thanks all, we'll keep monitoring and report back if it recurs. :thumbsup:

raj: Closing loop — created internal todo to add a header-preservation unit test and add a temporary metric to catch Authorization==undefined on replays.

acme-frontend: FYI if it helps, we also saw a related flaky case when using service worker fetch in Safari; different cause, but worth noting.

sam: Noted. Thanks for the detailed repro, huge help.
